The shipped example shows the\n14\tshape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then\n15\tcasts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader\n16\tthat `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. That is the careful version,\n17\twritten by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a\n18\tconfidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.\n19\t\n20\tThe registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer\n21\tto implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —\n41\tit does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and\n42\tthere is no opt-out flag.\n43\t\n44\tUpdate `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.\n45\t\n46\t## Acceptance criteria\n47\t\n48\t- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's\n49\t      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse`\n50\t      whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked\n51\t- [ ] A new `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` (the registry has no test file today)\n52\t      registers a tool requiring a `location` string, calls `execute` with `{}`, and\n53\t      asserts the returned result names `location` as required and the executor's call\n54\t      count is `0`\n55\t- [ ] A test asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the\n56\t      executor unchanged (`toEqual`, so an added default or coerced value fails the test) —\n57\t      exactly once\n58\t- [ ] A test asserts a wrong-typed field (a number where a string is required) is rejected\n59\t      with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does\n60\t      **not** contain the offending value\n61\t- [ ] A test asserts `register` throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and\n62\t      that the thrown message names the tool\n63\t- [ ] A test asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between\n64\t      calls is validated against the schema current at that call, not a stale cached one\n65\t- [ ] A test asserts a static tool's schema is compiled once across ten `execute` calls\n66\t- [ ] A tool-loop test in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts` drives a stub provider through a\n67\t      rejected tool call followed by a corrected retry, and asserts `processMessage`\n68\t      resolves — not rejects — with the rejection text visible to the provider on the next\n69\t      round\n70\t- [ ] `execute` still throws `Unknown tool: <name>` for an unregistered name, unchanged,\n71\t      pinned by a test\n72\t- [ ] Rejection messages and log lines name the failing property paths and the constraint\n73\t      that failed, and never a property **value**. Only the\n * OUTERMOST member expression of a chain is reported — an inner one whose\n * parent continues the chain (as the object of another member, or as the\n * callee of a call that is itself continued) is skipped.\n *\n * Exempt:\n *  - the root is `this` / `super`;\n *  - the root is a well-known global (`Math`, `JSON`, `Promise`, `Object`,\n *    `Array`, `Number`, `String`, `Reflect`, `process`, `console`,\n *    `globalThis`, `window`, `document`, `Symbol`, `Date`) or a name listed\n *    in option `allowRoots`;\n *  - every hop after the root is a call (`builder().a().b().c()` fluent\n *    chains return the same kind of thing at each step);\n *  - chains rooted in `import.meta`.\n *\n * Detect-only: the fix is a method on the direct collaborator.\n */\nconst DEFAULT_MAX = 2;\nconst CHAIN_TEXT_LIMIT = 60;\nconst DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ROOTS = new Set([\n    \"Math\",\n    \"JSON\",\n    \"Promise\",\n    \"Object\",\n    \"Array\",\n    \"Number\",\n    \"String\",\n    \"Reflect\",\n    \"process\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"globalThis\",\n    \"window\",\n    \"document\",\n    \"Symbol\",\n    \"Date\",\n]);\nconst EXEMPT_ROOT_TYPES = new Set([\"ThisExpression\", \"Super\", \"MetaProperty\"]);\nconst TRANSPARENT_WRAPPERS = new Set([\n    \"ChainExpression\",\n    \"TSNonNullExpression\",\n]);\nfunction isCalled(node) {\n    const parent = node.parent;\n    return (Boolean(parent) &&\n        parent.type === \"CallExpression\" &&\n        parent.callee === node);\n}\nfunction continuesChain(node) {\n    const parent = node.parent;\n    if (!parent) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (parent.type === \"MemberExpression\") {\n        return parent.object === node;\n    }\n    const isTransparentWrapper = isCalled(node) || TRANSPARENT_WRAPPERS.has(parent.type);\n    return isTransparentWrapper && continuesChain(parent);\n}\n/** The node a call or transparent wrapper is applied to; null for anything else. */\nfunction wrappedOf(node) {\n    if (node.type === \"CallExpression\") {\n        return node.callee;\n    }\n    return TRANSPARENT_WRAPPERS.has(node.type) ? node.expression : null;\n}\nfunction unwrapToMember(node) {\n    let current = node;\n    while (current.type !== \"MemberExpression\") {\n        current = wrappedOf(current);\n        if (!current) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n    return current;\n}\nfunction measureChain(outer) {\n    let hops = 0;\n    let everyHopCalled = true;\n    let current = outer;\n    while (current) {\n        hops += 1;\n        everyHopCalled = everyHopCalled && isCalled(current);\n        const inner = unwrapToMember(current.object);\n        if (!inner) {\n            return { hops, everyHopCalled, root: rootOf(current.object) };\n        }\n        current = inner;\n    }\n    return { hops, everyHopCalled, root: null };\n}\nfunction rootOf(node) {\n    let current = node;\n    while (current.type === \"CallExpression\" ||\n        current.type === \"TSNonNullExpression\") {\n        current =\n            current.type === \"CallExpression\" ? current.callee : current.expression;\n    }\n    return current;\n}\nfunction isExemptRoot(root, allowedRoots) {\n    if (EXEMPT_ROOT_TYPES.has(root.type)) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    return root.type === \"Identifier\" && allowedRoots.has(root.name);\n}\nfunction reportData(node, hops, max, sourceCode) {\n    const text = sourceCode.getText(node);\n    const chain = text.length > CHAIN_TEXT_LIMIT\n        ? `${text.slice(0, CHAIN_TEXT_LIMIT - 3)}...`\n        : text;\n    return { chain, depth: String(hops), max: String(max) };\n}\nexport default {\n    meta: {\n        type: \"suggestion\",\n        docs: {\n            description: \"Enforce a maximum member-access chain depth (Law of Demeter); fluent all-call chains, this, and well-known globals are exempt\",\n        },\n        schema: [\n            {\n                type: \"object\",\n                properties: {\n                    max: { type: \"integer\", minimum: 1 },\n                    allowRoots: { type: \"array\", items: { type: \"string\" } },\n                },\n                additionalProperties: false,\n            },\n        ],\n        messages: {\n            chainTooDeep: \"Member chain '{{chain}}' reaches {{depth}} hops deep (max {{max}}); ask the direct collaborator for what you need\",\n        },\n    },\n    create(context) {\n        const options = context.options[0] ?? {};\n        const max = options.max ?? DEFAULT_MAX;\n        const allowedRoots = new Set([\n            ...DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ROOTS,\n            ...(options.allowRoots ?? []),\n        ]);\n        const sourceCode = context.sourceCode;\n        return {\n            MemberExpression(node) {\n                if (continuesChain(node)) {\n                    return;\n                }\n                const { hops, everyHopCalled, root } = measureChain(node);\n                if (hops <= max || everyHopCalled || isExemptRoot(root, allowedRoots)) {\n                    return;\n                }\n                context.report({\n                    node,\n                    messageId: \"chainTooDeep\",\n                    data: reportData(node, hops, max, sourceCode),\n                });\n            },\n        };\n    },\n};\n","numLines":165,"startLine":1,"totalLines":165}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_9773684f1e20410082c2fd5c","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_9d348242131a4a668f8e6411","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Tool Input Validation\n2\t\n3\t| Field  | Value                |\n4\t| ------ | -------------------- |\n5\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n6\t| Status | In Progress          |\n7\t\n8\tEvery tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n9\t\n10\t## Validation at execute time\n11\t\n12\t- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).\n13\t- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n14\t- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults.\n15\t- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.\n16\t\n17\t## Schema compilation and caching\n18\t\n19\t- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: throws at registration time naming the tool for an uncompilable schema](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L4)).\n20\t- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema`.\n21\t- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules.\n22\t\n23\t## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n24\t\n25\t- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).\n26\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db018f3f-74f7-478f-ac55-5c2898892206","uuid":"e5133112-726e-43df-b32d-c09332d45c36","timestamp":"2026-10-30T19:55:22.578Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/ec47987a64fe/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md","content":"# Tool Input Validation\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n| Status | In Progress          |\n\nEvery tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n\n## Validation at execute time\n\n- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).\n- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults.\n- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.\n\n## Schema compilation and caching\n\n- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: throws at registration time naming the tool for an uncompilable schema](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L4)).\n- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema`.\n- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules.\n\n## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n\n- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).\n","numLines":26,"startLine":1,"totalLines":26}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_9d348242131a4a668f8e6411","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

async () => {\n    const registry = new ToolRegistry();\n    let executorCalls = 0;\n    registry.register(\n      {\n        name: 'get_weather',\n        description: 'Get weather for a location',\n        inputSchema: {\n          type: 'object',\n          properties: {location: {type: 'string'}},\n          required: ['location'],\n        },\n      },\n      async () => {\n Ajv from 'ajv';\nimport type {ValidateFunction} from 'ajv';\nimport type {ToolDefinition} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n\nexport interface ToolResponse {\n  result: string;\n  clientMessages?: OutgoingMessage[];\n  suppressAssistantResponse?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface ToolContext {\n  userId: string | number;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  workspaceId?: string | number;\n  authHeaders?: {\n    cookie?: string;\n    authorization?: string;\n    host?: string;\n  };\n}\n\nexport type ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;\n\nexport function normalizeToolResponse(response: string | ToolResponse): ToolResponse {\n  return typeof response === 'string' ? {result: response} : response;\n}\n\nexport type ToolDefinitionSource = ToolDefinition | (() => ToolDefinition);\n\nexport interface RegisteredTool {\n  definition: ToolDefinition;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n}\n\ninterface StoredTool {\n  definitionSource: ToolDefinitionSource;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n  staticValidator: ValidateFunction | undefined;\n}\n\nexport class ToolRegistry {\n  private readonly tools = new Map<string, StoredTool>();\n  private readonly dynamicValidators = new WeakMap<Record<string, unknown>, ValidateFunction>();\n\n  private resolveDefinition(source: ToolDefinitionSource): ToolDefinition {\n    return typeof source === 'function' ? source() : source;\n  }\n\n  register(definition: ToolDefinitionSource, execute: ToolExecutor): void {\n    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(definition);\n    const staticValidator =\n      typeof definition === 'function' ? undefined : compileSchema(resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n    this.tools.set(resolved.name, {definitionSource: definition, execute, staticValidator});\n  }\n\n  get(name: string): RegisteredTool | undefined {\n    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) return undefined;\n    return {definition: this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource), execute: tool.execute};\n  }\n\n  getDefinitions(): ToolDefinition[] {\n    return [...this.tools.values()].map(t => this.resolveDefinition(t.definitionSource));\n  }\n\n  getPromptInstructions(): string[] {\n    return this.getDefinitions()\n      .filter(t => t.promptInstructions)\n      .map(t => `${t.name}: ${t.promptInstructions}`);\n  }\n\n  getExamplePrompts(): string[] {\n    return this.getDefinitions().flatMap(t => t.examplePrompts ?? []);\n  }\n\n  has(name: string): boolean {\n    return this.tools.has(name);\n  }\n\n  /** Rejection ToolResponse for input the schema rejects; throw only for an unknown tool name (specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md). */\n  async execute(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext): Promise<ToolResponse> {\n    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'tool not found', {name});\n      throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);\n    }\n    const validateInput = this.validatorFor(tool);\n    if (!validateInput(input)) {\n      const problems = (validateInput.errors ?? [])\n        .map(error => `${error.instancePath || 'input'} ${error.message}`)\n        .join('; ');\n      log.warn('tool', 'input rejected by inputSchema', {name, problems});\n      return {result: `Tool input rejected: ${problems}`};\n    }\n    log.info('tool', 'executing', {name, inputKeys: Object.keys(input)});\n    const rawResult = await tool.execute(input, context);\n    const response = normalizeToolResponse(rawResult);\n    log.info('tool', 'execution complete', {\n      name,\n      rawType: typeof rawResult,\n      clientMessageCount: response.clientMessages?.length ?? 0,\n      clientMessageTypes: response.clientMessages?.map(m => m.type) ?? [],\n      suppressAssistantResponse: response.suppressAssistantResponse ?? false,\n    });\n    return response;\n  }\n\n  private validatorFor(tool: StoredTool): ValidateFunction {\n    const staticValidator = tool.staticValidator;\n    if (staticValidator) return staticValidator;\n    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource);\n    const cached = this.dynamicValidators.get(resolved.inputSchema);\n    if (cached) return cached;\n    const compiled = compileSchema(resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n    this.dynamicValidators.set(resolved.inputSchema, compiled);\n    return compiled;\n  }\n}\n\nconst ajv = new Ajv({strict: false, validateFormats: false, allErrors: true});\n\nfunction compileSchema(toolName: string, schema: Record<string, unknown>): ValidateFunction {\n  try {\n    return ajv.compile(schema);\n  } catch (error) {\n    throw new Error(`Invalid inputSchema for tool \"${toolName}\": ${(error as Error).message}`, {cause: error});\n  }\n}\n","numLines":131,"startLine":1,"totalLines":131}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_1c1563a0f56740adae8e177c","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
